text: Genesis 6 sets a world corrupt all the way down beside one man who "walked with God" (6:9). The narrator makes no effort to soften the corruption. "Every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually" (6:5), "the earth was filled with violence" (6:11), and Yahweh "repented" that he had made man (6:6). Noah receives no commission to reform any of this. His commission is to build. More of the chapter goes to the ark's specifications (gopher wood, rooms, pitch, length, breadth, height, window, door, and three decks in 6:14–16) than to the corruption that makes the ark necessary, because Noah builds to a measure he did not set. The ark exists as dimensions before it exists as wood. Of Noah's part the narrator says only this: "according to all that God commanded him, so did he" (6:22). Noah is called righteous in 6:9, before he does anything. In the chapter his righteousness becomes visible as obedience, the willingness to build what God, who "looked upon the earth" and saw all flesh corrupted (6:12), says will be needed.
